newsitem.title: QATAR: Deals worth $25 million concluded at Qatar show.
newsitem.headline: Deals worth $25 million concluded at Qatar show.

text.p: Business deals worth $25 million were concluded on the sidelines of an international police and security equipment exhibition in Qatar on Monday, a senior Qatari police official said.
"Two deals were made with two German companies and one with an American company", Lieutenant Colonel Mohamed Youssef Almana, head of Milipol Qatar 96 exhibition, told Reuters.

Under a $10 million deal, the Munich-based Maha-Export is to supply car safety testing equipment to Qatar's traffic department. Under a $3 million deal, Germany's Erich Utsch company will supply the department with car number plates.

The third deal, valued at $12 million, was reached between Qatar's armed forces and the United States' AM General Corporation, which will supply 30 high mobility multi-purpose wheeled vehicles, called 'Hummer', within six months from January 1997.
Lt Col Almana said discussions were also under way with IBM to supply dictation devices to Qatar's central bank and Motorola to supply telecommunications equipment to Qatar's government.
Some 187 companies from 24 countries are participating in the show, which ends on Tuesday.
